title: Personal Credit Cards: points available on a card for a points statement credit
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: points available for paying down the card with points

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder uses rewards points to pay down what a card owes through a statement credit on that card, it fixes how many points the card has available to draw on.

## Rule

The available points are counted from the card's ledger at handling time:

- all points posted by the card's earning entries,
- less all points posted by the card's redemption entries,
- less all points posted by the card's forfeiture entries, including removals that take back the points of a refunded purchase.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** every earning, redemption and forfeiture entry on this card's ledger, as it stands at handling time.
- **Judgement:** total the points of each kind, then take the redemption total and the forfeiture total away from the earning total.
- **Output:** the points available on the card.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger)

A card whose earning entries total 30500 points, whose redemption entries total 4000 points and whose forfeiture entries total 1500 points has 30500 less 4000 less 1500, that is 25000 points available.

## Points of judgement

- A redemption posted earlier in the same handling is part of the ledger at handling time and lowers the available points.
- The count is taken from the ledger entries of this card only.
- The figure comes from the ledger entries themselves; no other points figure replaces it.
